## Finding

On r17200, `sdcc -mmcs51 --model-large -c width.c` stops with an internal error for the file
below, whose bit-field width is a conditional expression.

```c
struct s { unsigned int a : 1 ? 3 : 4; };
struct s v;
```

The compiler prints `Internal error: validateLink failed in SPEC_SCLS(cexpr->etype)` and
`expected SPECIFIER, got null-link` for line 2223 of `src/SDCCast.c`, with each of the six mcs51
option sets of the regression suite. The compiler of r17193 prints it for line 2211. Only mcs51
was compiled without the patch.

The widths `0 ? 3 : 5`, `_Generic (1, int : 6, default : 1.0)`, `W > 2 ? W : 1` with an
enumeration constant `W`, and `MAX (3, 2)` with the macro `((a) > (b) ? (a) : (b))` get the
internal error too, and so do unnamed bit-fields with such widths. The width `0 ? 3 : -1` gets it
in place of error 363 (`negative bit-field size`). The widths `3` and `sizeof (char) + 2` compile.

## Cause

The two `member_declarator` rules for bit-fields in `src/SDCC.y` call `constExprValue` twice with
the tree of the width, for `ulFromVal` and for `floatFromVal` in the test for a negative width.
`constExprValue` in `src/SDCCast.c` continues with the tree that `decorateType` returns. For a
conditional operator with a constant condition, `decorateType` returns the operand that is
selected, and for `_Generic` the expression of the association that is chosen. The root that the
rule has is then marked as decorated and does not have a type. In the second call,
`decorateType` returns this root unchanged, and `validateLink` reports the null `etype` at
`SPEC_SCLS (cexpr->etype)`. For `+`, `decorateType` writes the constant into the root itself,
which is why `sizeof (char) + 2` compiles.

## Fix

Each of the two rules calls `constExprValue` once and passes its value to both functions.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bitfield-width-expr.c` checks the size and the position of bit-fields
with such widths. `support/valdiag/tests/bitfield-width-expr.c` has two cases with valid widths
and two that expect an error for the widths `0 ? 3 : -1` and `1 ? -2 : 2`. On r17200 without the
patch, the compiler stops with the internal error at the regression test for the six mcs51
variants, and the two cases that expect an error fail for mcs51, mcs51-large, and
mcs51-stack-auto.

With the patch series of this report applied to r17200, both tests pass. The regression suite has
0 failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80, and the diagnostics suite has 0
failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. The patch was not run on r17200
without the other patches of the series.

## Related

- In bug #4228, `decorateType` replaces the root of the initializer of a constexpr object or of a
  compound literal in this way. [r17196](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/17196/) fixed it
  with copies of the initializer, and it does not change the `member_declarator` rules.
- With the other patches of this report on r17200 and without this one, the widths under Finding
  get error 2 (`Initializer element is not a constant expression`) for mcs51, because the patch
  for bug #3971 tests `IS_AST_SYM_VALUE (cexpr)` in front of `SPEC_SCLS (cexpr->etype)`.
- The width `w > 2 ? w : 1` after `constexpr int w = 3;` gets error 2 on r17200 in front of the
  internal error, and on r17193 with the two changes of this patch error 2 is its only error.
